bill_name: Measures for Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content
bill_summary: Joint measures by CAC, MIIT, MPS, and NRTA requiring explicit and implicit labeling of AI-generated/synthetic content (text, images, audio, video). Took effect September 1, 2025.

bill_name: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation for Trust (AI Basic Act)
bill_summary: First comprehensive national AI framework law in Asia. Establishes AI governance, promotes AI industry, requires high-impact AI impact assessments, creates AI Safety Research Institute. Promulgated Jan 21, 2025; entered into force Jan 22, 2026.

bill_name: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technologies (AI Promotion Act)
bill_summary: Japan's first national AI law. Establishes an AI Strategic Headquarters chaired by the Prime Minister, mandates an AI Basic Plan, and promotes R&D with light-touch coordination rather than prohibitions. Passed Diet May 28, 2025; promulgated June 4, 2025.

bill_name: Law 132/2025: Provisions and Delegations to the Government on Artificial Intelligence
bill_summary: Italy's national AI law complementing the EU AI Act. Covers national strategy, governance (AGID and ACN as supervisory authorities), copyright protection, AI in workplaces, and delegates implementing decrees. Published in Official Gazette Sept 25, 2025.

bill_name: India AI Governance Guidelines
bill_summary: Non-binding governance framework issued by MeitY under the IndiaAI Mission. Proposes AI Governance Group, AI Safety Institute, risk classification framework, and techno-legal approach rather than immediate new legislation.

bill_name: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
bill_summary: Voluntary code prepared by 13 independent experts with 1000+ stakeholders to help GPAI model providers comply with the AI Act's transparency, copyright, and safety obligations. Published July 10, 2025.

bill_name: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules 2025
bill_summary: Amends IT Rules 2021 to require labeling of synthetically generated content (deepfakes), user declarations for AI content on social media, senior-level oversight for content takedowns, and technical measures to verify declarations. Effective November 1, 2025.

bill_name: Measures for the Security Management of Facial Recognition Technology Applications
bill_summary: Joint measures by CAC and MPS regulating facial recognition technology. Prohibits forcing individuals to use facial recognition as sole verification, bans cameras in private spaces, requires impact assessments. Effective June 1, 2025.

bill_name: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
bill_summary: Vietnam's comprehensive AI law with 8 chapters and 35 articles. Establishes risk management framework, prohibits certain AI practices, creates National AI Development Fund, includes regulatory sandboxes. Passed with 90.7% approval. Effective March 1, 2026.

bill_name: EU AI Act - Prohibited Practices and AI Literacy (Article 5 & Article 4 application)
bill_summary: First provisions of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) became applicable: bans on unacceptable-risk AI practices (social scoring, manipulative AI, untargeted facial scraping, real-time biometric ID) and AI literacy obligations for providers and deployers.

bill_name: EU AI Act - GPAI Model Rules and Governance Provisions
bill_summary: EU AI Act provisions on general-purpose AI model obligations, governance structure (AI Office, AI Board), and penalties became applicable on August 2, 2025.

bill_name: Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
bill_summary: First formal amendment to the EU AI Act. Delays high-risk AI obligations (Annex III to Dec 2027, Annex I to Aug 2028), extends SME simplifications, expands regulatory sandboxes, removes AI literacy as binding obligation, and grants AI Office extended oversight powers.

bill_name: AI Liability Directive (Withdrawn)
bill_summary: Proposed directive to harmonize non-contractual civil liability rules for AI. Would have eased burden of proof for claimants harmed by AI systems. Formally withdrawn by the Commission in October 2025 due to lack of foreseeable agreement among institutions.

bill_name: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA, part of Bill C-27)
bill_summary: Canada's proposed AI regulation establishing a risk-based framework for high-impact AI systems. Died on the Order Paper when Parliament was prorogued on January 6, 2025, following Prime Minister Trudeau's resignation announcement.

bill_name: Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024 (Commencement)
bill_summary: Prohibits publication of digitally generated or manipulated content (including AI deepfakes) depicting election candidates saying/doing things they did not. Empowers Returning Officer to issue corrective directions. Came into operation January 22, 2025.

bill_name: AI Basic Act Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 36053)
bill_summary: Enforcement Decree providing operational details for the AI Basic Act, including criteria for high-impact AI, foreign entity representative designation, and AI industry support measures. Approved by Cabinet January 20, 2026; entered into force January 22, 2026.

bill_name: Criminal Code Amendment (Deepfake Sexual Material) Act 2024
bill_summary: Strengthens Criminal Code offences for creating and sharing non-consensual sexual material online, including material created or altered using AI technology (deepfakes). Passed both houses August 2024; received Royal Assent September 2024; commenced early 2025.

bill_name: Gesetz zur Durchführung der Verordnung über künstliche Intelligenz (KI-MIG)
bill_summary: Germany's AI Act implementation law. Designates Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA) as central AI market surveillance authority and coordinating body, establishes KI-Kompetenz- und Koordinierungszentrum. Does not add substantive obligations beyond the EU AI Act.

bill_name: Laki eräiden tekoälyjärjestelmien valvonnasta (Act on Supervision of Certain AI Systems, 1377/2025)
bill_summary: Finland's national implementation of the EU AI Act. Designates market surveillance authorities and fundamental rights authorities, establishes supervisory powers. Approved by President of the Republic on December 22, 2025; entered into force January 1, 2026.

bill_name: European Union (Artificial Intelligence) (Designation) Regulations 2025 (SI No. 366 of 2025)
bill_summary: Designates 15 national competent authorities (including Central Bank, Data Protection Commission, Health and Safety Authority) as market surveillance authorities for the EU AI Act in Ireland. Minister for Enterprise designated as single point of contact.

bill_name: Ustawa o systemach sztucznej inteligencji (Act on AI Systems)
bill_summary: Poland's AI Act implementation law. Establishes the Commission for the Development and Safety of Artificial Intelligence (KRiBSI) as the sole market surveillance authority, creates regulatory sandboxes, and implements EU AI Act enforcement provisions.

bill_name: Bill 2338/2023 - AI Regulatory Framework (passed by Senate)
bill_summary: Comprehensive AI regulation bill establishing rights for affected persons, risk-based obligations, national governance architecture (SIA), and sanctions. Passed by Senate December 2024; transmitted to Chamber of Deputies March 2025. Currently under review in special committee.

bill_name: Bill 16821-19 Regulating AI Systems (passed by Chamber of Deputies)
bill_summary: Comprehensive AI regulation bill inspired by EU AI Act. Establishes risk-based framework, prohibits unacceptable-risk practices, creates sanctions regime with fines up to 20,000 UTM. Passed Chamber of Deputies October 13, 2025; now in Senate.

bill_name: Artificial Intelligence Basic Act
bill_summary: Taiwan's first AI framework law, promulgated on 14 January 2026, establishing seven governance principles (sustainability, human autonomy, privacy, cybersecurity, transparency, fairness, accountability). It designates the NSTC as the central competent authority and tasks the government with creating a risk classification framework within 24 months.

bill_name: Federal Council Decision on AI Regulatory Approach and Council of Europe AI Convention Ratification
bill_summary: The Swiss Federal Council decided on 12 February 2025 to ratify the Council of Europe AI Convention and adopted a sector-specific regulatory approach rather than a comprehensive AI Act. Switzerland subsequently signed the Convention on 27 March 2025. A consultation draft is expected by end of 2026.

bill_name: Guidelines for Ensuring the Appropriateness of R&D and Utilization of AI-Related Technology
bill_summary: Issued by the AI Strategic Headquarters on 19 December 2025 pursuant to Article 13 of the AI Act. These guidelines set out a risk-based approach and recommend practices for government, businesses, and citizens to ensure appropriate AI development and use. They remain non-binding soft law.

bill_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
bill_summary: Notified on 13 November 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)), the DPDP Rules operationalize India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The Rules impose phased compliance obligations including algorithmic fairness assessments for Significant Data Fiduciaries, 72-hour breach reporting, and specific consent requirements directly applicable to AI systems processing personal data.

bill_name: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 230-VIII)
bill_summary: Kazakhstan became the first Central Asian state with a dedicated AI statute when the President signed Law No. 230-VIII on 17 November 2025 (in force 18 January 2026). It establishes a risk-based framework, bans social scoring and manipulative AI, mandates labeling of synthetic content, and creates a National AI Platform.

bill_name: Law on Introducing Amendments to Certain Legislative Acts in Connection with AI Regulation (Law No. ZRU-1115)
bill_summary: Uzbekistan's first AI-focused legislation, entering into force on 21 January 2026. It amends the Law on Informatization to add Article 71 on AI use in information resources and introduces administrative liability (fines 50-100 BCU) for unlawful processing of personal data using AI technologies.

bill_name: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
bill_summary: Published by IMDA on 22 January 2026 at the World Economic Forum, this is the world's first comprehensive governance framework for agentic AI. It covers risk bounding, human accountability, technical controls, and end-user responsibility. Though voluntary, it serves as the reference standard for AI governance across Southeast Asia.

bill_name: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 - Section 80 (Automated Decision-Making)
bill_summary: Section 80 of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, which replaced Article 22 of the UK GDPR with new Articles 22A-22D on automated decision-making, came into force on 5 February 2026. The reforms expand the lawful bases for solely automated decisions while requiring safeguards including transparency, human review, and the right to contest.

bill_name: Council Decision (EU) 2026/1080 on the Conclusion of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
bill_summary: The European Union deposited its instrument of ratification of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225) on 15 May 2026 at the 135th Session of the Committee of Ministers in Chisinau. The EU declared it will apply the Convention through the EU AI Act and related acquis.

bill_name: Establishment of the Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data
bill_summary: Announced on 14 June 2026, the UAE established the Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data, consolidating the AI Office, TDRA's digital government sector, and the Emirates Data Office into a single body reporting directly to the Cabinet. It is the first federal-level cabinet-reporting AI authority in the GCC.

bill_name: Digital Economy and AI Content Regulation Law
bill_summary: Ratified by the UAE Federal National Council in June 2026 and entering into force on 1 September 2026, this is the GCC's first comprehensive federal law governing AI-generated media. It mandates standardized labeling of AI-generated content, requires data broker registration, and imposes fines up to AED 5 million per violation.

bill_name: DIFC Data Protection Regulations - Regulation 10 (Autonomous Systems)
bill_summary: DIFC Regulation 10, the first AI-specific regulation in the MEASA region, reached full enforcement on 1 January 2026. It imposes strict liability, transparency, and audit requirements on entities deploying autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems that process personal data within the Dubai International Financial Centre jurisdiction.

bill_name: SDAIA Package of 10 AI Regulatory Guidance Documents
bill_summary: On 8 June 2026, SDAIA announced a package of 10 regulatory guidance documents covering AI ethics principles, generative AI guidelines for government and public use, and deepfake guidelines. While non-binding, these function as the operative regulatory baseline for Saudi Arabia's Year of AI 2026, supplemented by the binding PDPL.

bill_name: Complementary Law No. 205/2025 - State Policy for Promoting AI Innovation (Goias)
bill_summary: Goias became the first Brazilian state to enact an AI-specific law on 19 May 2025. Complementary Law 205/2025 establishes a state AI innovation policy with principles including ethics, transparency, security, and open-source preference. It creates an Ethics and Innovation in AI nucleus, a permanent regulatory sandbox, and regulates autonomous agents and edge AI.

bill_name: Work Health and Safety Amendment (Digital Work Systems) Act 2026 (NSW)
bill_summary: Passed by both houses of NSW Parliament (assent received 18 February 2026), this is the first Australian legislation to impose express WHS duties on employers using AI, algorithms, automation, and digital work platforms. It requires PCBUs to manage risks from algorithmic work allocation including excessive workloads, unreasonable monitoring, and discriminatory algorithmic decisions.

bill_name: Withdrawal of Draft South Africa National AI Policy
bill_summary: On 4 June 2026, South Africa's Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies withdrew the Draft National AI Policy (published 10 April 2026) in its entirety. The withdrawal followed revelations that the policy was drafted using AI which hallucinated at least six citations. A seven-member expert panel was appointed to guide a redraft.

bill_name: AI Basic Act Amendment (Public Sector AI Procurement)
bill_summary: A revision to South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 21 July 2026, creating a public demand system requiring national and local governments to prioritize AI products in procurement. It also expands AI-vulnerable group eligibility and supports costs of AI services for additional populations including women with career interruptions.
